unit.why: A single anecdote: the Yehudi's wife asks R. Simha Bunem to write to her husband about her bleeding and lack of money, and he writes a cryptic letter that only the Yehudi can decipher.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי שהיה היהודי ז"ל אצל הרבי
stories.summary_en: While the Yehudi is with the Seer in Lublin, his wife asks R. Simha Bunem to write to him about heavy menstrual bleeding and her lack of money; Bunem writes a cryptic letter built on the double sense of 'damim' (blood / money), which only the Yehudi understands.

tags.why: The Yehudi's wife (the rebbetzin) sets the plot in motion.

quotes: ובאה אל הרה״ק ר׳ שמחה בונם זצ״ל
tags.why: The wife acts by coming and making the request, but the story centres on the letter.

quotes: איך שהולכים ממנה דמים הרבה מן הווסת
tags.why: Her complaint triggers the letter and the wordplay.
The letter plays on niddah (menstrual) blood and on a Talmudic legal formula.

quotes: דמים תרתי משמע אחד המרבה ואחד הממעיט
tags.why: The letter is a witty, punning rendering of a serious complaint.

quotes: ושום אדם לא יכול להבין הפי' באגרת עד שהיהודי ז״ל קרא
tags.why: The coded exchange between the master (the Yehudi) and his disciple (Bunem) only the two of them understand.
The wife's intimate and material needs are relayed to her absent husband.

quotes: שהיה היהודי ז"ל אצל הרבי זצ"ל בלובלין
tags.why: The setting is the Yehudi's stay with the Seer of Lublin.

missing_concepts: cryptic letter / wordplay (double meaning of דמים) understood only by the master
menstrual irregularity as a marital/health concern
material want of the tsaddik's household
